Republic of the Philippines DEPARTMENT OF THE INTERIOR AND LOCAL GOVERNMENT A. Francisco Gold Condominium II Bldg, EDSA corner Mapagmahal St., Diliman, Quezon City LEGAL SERVICE DILG OPINION NO. 29 S. 19 March 2010 HON. ANTONIO P. LUCERO Vice Governor and Presiding Officer Provincial Capitol Building Catarman, Northern Samar Dear Sir: This has reference to your letter interposing the following quoted queries, 2010 to wit: 1. 2. 3. "Under Article X, Section 4 of the Constitution, the President exercises general supervision over all Local Government Units (LGUs), including provinces. This power has been delegated to the Secretary of Interior and Local Government by virtue of the Local Government Code of 1991. Is the Sangguniang Panlalawigan of Northern Samar, an instrumentality of the province of Northern Samar, which is an LGU, bound to implement a Resolution or an appointment pursuant to such resolution of the National Executive Board of the Liga ng mga Barangay without the endorsement or directive of the Secretary of Interior and Local Government? As stated in the above antecedents, a TRO has been issued by the Court of Appeals against the National Executive Board of the Liga ng mga Barangay concerning Honorable Beda M Bogtong's right to office as President of the Provincial Liga Chapter. If the answer to the previous query is in the affirmative, what effect, if any, does the TRO have on the appointment of Mr. Victorio Singzon II and on the resolution of the National Executive Board? Is the appointment of Mr. Singzon as Acting President of the Northern Samar Provincial Liga Chapter by the NEB pursuant to

4. 5. 6. Article IX, Section 4 last sentence of paragraph 2 of the 2002 Liga Election Code valid? Does it not violate the TRO? If the appointment is invalid, is the Honorable Beda M. Bogtong, the incumbent Liga President, legally entitled to continue representing the Provincial Liga in the SP of Northern Samar in a hold-over capacity pursuant to Sections 3, 4 and 5 of the 2002 Liga Election Code? In the negative, is the incumbent Vice President (in descending order from the Executive Vice President down to the 3rd Vice President), legally entitled to assume the office of the Liga President, and perform all the duties and responsibilities required of a president under 2002 Election Code and Liga Constitution, until his successor is confirmed. In the event any of the incumbent Vice President also fails to get re-elected, are the remaining incumbent officers and members of the board legally entitled to elect from among themselves their representative to the local sanggunian? Is it correct to say that it is only in case of failure to election among themselves, that the National Liga can appoint a caretaker of the chapter concerned with the designation of Acting President?" Your queries have been impelled by the on-going controversy regarding the Liga ng mga Barangay Provincial Federation presidency involving Mr. Beda Bogtong, on one side, and the Liga itself, on the other. Records disclose that a case is now pending before the Court of Appeals, 20th Division, Cebu City and docketed as CA-G.R. SP No. 04746, entitled: "Beda M. Bogtong vs. National Executive Board (Liga ng mga Barangay sa Pilipinas, et Be that as it may, in reply to your first query, please be informed that in "Drilon vs. Lim" (G.R. No. 112497, 04 August 1994), the Supreme Court distinguished the term control and supervision, "the first being the power of an officer to alter or modify or set aside what a subordinate officer had done in the performance of his duties and to substitute the judgment of the former for the latter, while the second is the power of a superior officer to see to it that lower officers perform their functions in accordance with law Parenthetically, in the case of "Bito-onon vs. Fernandez" (G.R. No. 139813, 31 January 2001), a case involving the Liga ng mga Barangay, the Supreme Court emphatically ruled that: "the DILG Secretary exercises only the power of supervision over local government units, and this power entails merely 2

seeing to it that subordinate officers perform their functions in accordance with law. The amendment of the rules and guidelines promulgated by the National Liga Board would in effect, be an exercise of the power of control" Verily, decisions and subsequent acts of the Liga National Executive Board are beyond this Department's domain, lest we be accused of controlling the Liga. As regards queries nos. 2 to 6, piease be informed that we have endorsed the same to the Honorable Court of Appeals, 20th Division, as well as the National Liga for their respective disposition as we do not intend to violate the sub-judice rule. We hope to have enlightened you on the matter. Very truly yours, By Authority of the Secretary: ATTY. JESUS B. Director III Legal:87/La copy furnished: Director Francisco C. Jose DILG Regional Office No. Tacloban City 3
